previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of poorly controlled type 1 diabetes, hypertension, depression, and alcohol abuse was admitted for hyperglycemia and a urinary tract infection. She presented with nausea, vomiting, and a blood glucose of 505 but no evidence of ketoacidosis. Urinalysis showed significant white blood cells, and culture confirmed pan-sensitive E. coli. She was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and transitioned to oral Bactrim for a five-day course. Her insulin regimen was intensified due to infection-related insulin resistance, increasing her Lantus dose from 25 to 30 units and adjusting mealtime Humalog doses. Her blood sugars stabilized, and she remained asymptomatic from a cardiac and psychiatric standpoint. She reported one month of sobriety supported by sertraline and naltrexone. She was discharged home with updated insulin instructions, completion of antibiotics, and close follow-up with her primary care provider and endocrinologist.

ACTIVE ISSUES  
=================  
# DKA:
Patient with known type 1 diabetes with multiple prior 
admissions for DKA presenting after ingesting large amounts of 
alcohol and not taking her insulin for the past 24 hours. Labs 
consistent with DKA with severe anion gap metabolic acidosis, 
hyperglycemia, ketonuria, hyperkalemia, and ___. Patient 
enrolled in the DKA pathway. She was aggressively fluid 
resuscitated w/ NS, 250mg of IV bicarb, and was loaded with 2 
doses of IV insulin and started on insulin gtt at 9 U/hr. 
Overnight in the FICU, she was continued on the DKA protocol and 
required a maximum of 43U/hr on the insulin drip then was 
decreased back to 13U/hr. Blood glucose normalized, anion gap 
closed and acidosis normalized. Was started on Glargine 30U SC 
QAM and Humalog SS QID. ___ was consulted. Continued on LR 
@200cc/hour upon transfer to floor. Blood glucose normalized, 
anion gap closed, and acidosis normalized on floor, insulin 
dosing was adjusted by ___. Patinet was seen by ___ 
prior to discharge and arrange for follow up within one week. 
A1c found to be 11%, representing poor control for some time. 
Patient agreed that she will discuss outpatient psych/counseling 
with PCP to better control depression and alcohol, which are the 
primary issues preventing her adherence to diabetes management. 

# Hyperkalemia:
Extracellular shift likely related to severe metabolic acidosis. 
Initial EKG concerning for tented T-waves. Patient received 2 
doses of calcium gluconate. Initiated potassium repletion once K 
dropped below 5.3. Monitored on tele. No further issues after 
transfer to floor. 

# ___:
Patient with known baseline of creatinine of 0.9-1.0.
Admitted with creatinine of 1.9 likely ___ pre-renal azotemia
from hypovolemia given her DKA. At this time, other causes of 
___
are low on the differential. Cr improved to 0.9 on floor after 
IVF in ICU and PO intake on floor. Restarted on home losartan 
prior to discharge. 

# Alcohol Abuse:
Patient with known history of alcohol abuse. Reports that she 
had been drinking heavily for few days prior to admission. Last 
drink was a few hours prior to admission (1 pint of vodka). No 
history of withdrawal seizures. Was placed on CIWA protocol, 
without scoring throughout admission. Was started on thiamine 
500mg IV q8 for three days, folic acid, MVI and transitioned to 
PO on the floor. Social work saw patient and providing resources 
in ICU, after which she declined further assistance but plans to 
follow up with AA. Held home naltrexone as patient appears to 
have been taking it inconsistently and did not benefit from it. 

# Troponinemia: Demand ischemia, resolved after initiation of 
DKA tx.

=================  
# HTN: Held amlodipine given soft blood pressures in ICU, held 
losartan given ___, continued metoprolol XL 25mg PO daily. 
Amlodipine and losartan restarted on floor after improvement in 
BP and Cr. 

# CAD primary prevention: Continued aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 
80mg PO QPM

# Depression: Continued sertraline

# Iron deficiency anemia: Continued ferrous sulfate
